facts.fact: WardheerNews reported on 26 September 2026 that internet and telephone services were severely disrupted across Tigray as fighting resumed: Ethio Telecom services were completely down, Safaricom partly working, and NetBlocks confirmed a regional disruption; who ordered it is contested (Reuters sources blamed Tigray's ruling authorities, a source close to the TPLF blamed the federal government), no end date or start date is given, and the date used is the document's publication date.

note: No fact: a regulator's notice denying a Starlink licence claim; a licence matter is other and no one is stated punished or cut.

systems.system: Proclamation No. 590/2008 on Freedom of the Mass Media and Access to Information
systems.country_label: Mass Media and Access to Information Proclamation

note: No fact: a 2008 media and access-to-information law (other), preamble only, with no repeal, cut or punishment stated.
Opinion piece on telecom liberalisation and digital infrastructure; states nothing on criticism of a named policy, cuts or blocks, or punishment for speech.

facts.fact: Amnesty International says Addis Standard managing editor Million Beyene was abducted by national intelligence agency members on 15 April 2026 and held two weeks without access to his lawyer or family, which it says appears linked to his journalism.

Human Rights Watch reports the Ethiopian Media Authority permanently suspended two Deutsche Welle correspondents, alleging noncompliance with media and hate speech laws, after a nine-correspondent suspension from 23 October 2025.
Human Rights Watch says police arrested at least six Ethiopian journalists in the five months to mid-December 2025, some held without charge.

note: The document states nothing this study asks for Ethiopia.
The 2020 Hate Speech and Disinformation Proclamation is a speech law with no one reported charged under it.

facts.fact: OONI data shows Ethiopia blocked access to Facebook, Telegram, TikTok and YouTube from 9 February 2023, with the blocks apparently lasting until 17 July 2023.
Access Now says new internet shutdowns in Tigray, Ethiopia, are raising fears that the population cut off for over two years during the civil war will be disconnected again.
Access Now lists Ethiopia among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.

CPJ reports that on 2 November 2026 the Ethiopian Media Authority suspended the registration of The Reporter's publisher indefinitely, covering its Amharic and English editions and digital platforms, for reports it said undermine national interests.

CPJ reports that two days before the 2 November 2026 suspension The Reporter published an editorial, 'Press Freedom Is Not A Luxury!', criticising authorities for treating independent reporting as a national security threat and calling for release of journalists held without charge.

note: The 2026 revocations for Addis Standard and Wazema Radio and the detentions are dated only to the year.

facts.fact: Freedom House reports localised connectivity restrictions continued in Amhara Region, citing Addis Standard's February 2026 report of phone and internet outages in North Shewa Zone.

Freedom House reports Ethiopian authorities revoked independent digital outlet Addis Standard's licence in February 2026, citing CPJ, and an Addis Standard editor was seized from its newsroom in April 2026.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 22 May 2025 a Fafen Zone court sentenced Jigjiga Television Network founder Ahmed Awga to two years under the 2020 anti-hate speech law after he aired an interview alleging police brutality.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that Harari editor Muhyidin Abdullahi Omar was arrested on 5 April 2025 and charged on 28 April with defamation and disinformation over Facebook posts alleging corruption.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that journalist Tesfalem Waldyes was arrested on 8 June 2025 in Addis Ababa and accused by police of spreading false information.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that police arrested seven Ethiopian Broadcasting Service journalists on 26-28 March 2025 over an aired episode and accused them of inciting conflict.
Global Voices cites Ethiopia's Zone 9 bloggers as prosecuted for their posts in 2014.
Shega cites a Center for Rights and Democracy report of at least 26 internet shutdowns in Ethiopia since 2016, with no date given for the latest.

note: Corruption charges against officials are not punishment for speech; nothing on criticism or cuts.
The document states nothing this study asks of this country.
